a: An LLM (Large Language Model) predicts text and can answer questions, write code, and reason over prompts.
A prompt is the input text you give a model to steer its response.
A token is a chunk of text the model processes. Billing and limits are often counted in tokens.
Temperature controls randomness. Lower = more focused; higher = more creative.
An embedding is a numeric vector that represents text (or other data) for search and similarity.
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) fetches relevant documents and feeds them to an LLM for grounded answers.
Fine-tuning continues training a model on your data so it better matches your domain or style.
Inference is running a trained model to produce outputs (predictions or generated text).
A neural network is a model made of layers of interconnected units that learn patterns from data.
Overfitting means the model memorizes training data and performs poorly on new data.
A dataset is the collection of examples used to train, validate, or test a model.
An API key is a secret token that identifies and authorizes a client calling an API.
